answer: An adversary who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the glacier history. Churn is counted in basalt, and harbor publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 8% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. A 420 account operation therefore ties up 28 million dollars of idle capital. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
